title: Choose Eurofolio’s visual world
question: Three directions use the same real portfolio facts. Choose the one that should become the product.

options.label: Capital Map
options.lineage: Scandinavian transit diagrams × securities ownership maps
options.thesis: Accounts become visible ownership rails: three institutions converge into one EUR total, then branch into assets and positions.
options.viewport: A left account rail feeds a large central EUR balance; the portfolio branches across the page into allocation and ranked holdings without card shells.
options.risk: The map logic must remain immediately readable rather than becoming decorative data art.

raised.raise: Fixed-place precision: all important values align and hold their decimal positions.
Explicit state: every source, date, and valuation state has a permanent labeled position.
Structural honesty: account relationships determine the layout rather than a generic page grid.

options.label: Custody Register
options.lineage: Nordic private-bank statements × exchange closing bulletins
options.thesis: A beautifully typeset custody statement makes the portfolio feel official, calm, and exceptionally legible.
options.viewport: A compact masthead, statement balance, account ledger, allocation strip, and ranked positions share one rigorous ruled sheet.
options.risk: It is the most familiar and safest direction, and could feel like a polished statement rather than a new product.

options.label: Quotation Specimen
options.thesis: The numerical typography is the interface: scale, weight, and alignment encode portfolio hierarchy before any container does.
options.viewport: The total occupies the upper field as a typographic instrument; accounts and holdings lock to an exposed baseline grid below it.
options.case: Matches Capital Map on clarity and exceeds it in typographic character, but explains account provenance less naturally.
options.risk: Extreme scale contrast can become poster-like if the utility details are not disciplined.

options.label: Settlement Counter
options.thesis: Every balance is a fixed-place instrument reading.
options.viewport: Three counter banks report the institutions and total like laboratory instruments.
options.case: Strong numerical drama, but retro equipment weakens the quiet trust expected from a daily portfolio tool.
options.kept: Fixed-place numeric precision and a single warm state color.
options.risk: Too easily reads as themed novelty.

options.label: Exposure Structure
options.thesis: Holdings and currencies appear as a visible network of counterbalanced exposures.
options.viewport: Account nodes support a central portfolio value through labeled holding and currency forces.
options.case: Expresses relationships boldly, but overstates causal structure and makes exact comparison slower.
options.kept: Let the data relationships—not arbitrary cards—determine composition.
options.risk: Can imply financial relationships the ledger does not actually model.

canonCard.label: Conventional fintech dashboard
canonCard.thesis: Rounded KPI cards, a blue line chart, allocation widgets, and a sortable holdings table—executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: A header above a four-card KPI row, chart-and-donut grid, and holdings table.
canonCard.risk: Immediately familiar and almost impossible to distinguish from generated finance dashboards.
